0.1.0.title: The first yapmod release
0.1.0.summary: yapmod is a modded desktop client for Yapper. This first release focuses on the basics: a real desktop window, a proper titlebar, and a place to grow from.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Yapper now runs in its own desktop window.
Added a custom macOS titlebar overlay.
Introduced the yapmod logo and desktop icons.

0.1.1.title: Modals and configuration
0.1.1.summary: This release adds the building blocks for customizing yapmod and showing dialogs over the Yapper interface.

sections.heading: New
items: Added a reusable modal API for injected scripts.
Added a welcome modal shown on the first launch.
Added a config file with options for the native titlebar and starting maximized.

0.1.2.title: A smoother first launch
0.1.2.summary: A small release focused on fixing rough edges and making the app easier to install and use.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: macOS builds are now ad-hoc signed, so the app opens without a damaged app warning.
The login screen now opens when you are not signed in.
Improved the README and release workflow.

sections.heading: New
items: Release notes now appear after an update, so you can see what changed.
The version you last ran is saved in your config file.

0.2.0.title: Settings, links, and a website
0.2.0.summary: This release puts yapmod's options where you expect them: inside Yapper's own settings page. It also adds an official website with direct downloads and makes external links open in your normal browser.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Added a Yapmod section to Yapper's settings, so desktop options live next to the rest of the app.
Added an official landing page with direct download links for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
External links now open in your default browser instead of inside the app.

sections.heading: New
items: The native titlebar and start-maximized options can now be toggled from the settings page, and apply on the next launch.
Settings are stored in your config file and can be written to from the injected page.
The release notes modal now shows the version, release date, and changelog of every past release.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Following a link to another site no longer opens a broken window inside the desktop client.

0.3.1.title: Notifications that arrive
0.3.1.summary: This release makes the desktop notifications and the unread badge work on every platform.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Desktop notifications now show up in the notification center of your system. The webview cannot post them by itself, so yapmod hands them over to the system.
The number of unread messages now reaches the app icon, on the Dock, the taskbar and the panel.

sections.heading: New
items: Added a Desktop notifications option and a Show the unread badge option to the yapmod section in the settings.
Clicking a notification brings yapmod to the front and opens the message it was about.

sections.heading: How it works
items: Yapper keeps deciding when to notify you: muted channels and servers, Do Not Disturb, and a window that is in front are all respected.

0.3.0.title: Notifications, voice calls, and updates
0.3.0.summary: This release adds notification and mention badges on every platform, fixes voice calls on macOS, and makes yapmod easier to keep up to date.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Unread and mention badges now show up on servers and channels, with desktop notifications and notification sounds on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Voice calls now work on macOS. The first time you join a call, allow microphone access and your mic is live.
yapmod now checks for updates and shows a notice when a newer version is available.

sections.heading: New
items: Added a changelog in settings, so you can read the notes for every release from inside the app.
Added a documentation site with full-text search for setup, troubleshooting, FAQ and developer docs.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: The previous settings panel no longer stays visible when you switch sections.
Settings from older yapmod versions are migrated correctly, so your window options survive an update.
The Linux app now uses the proper Tux icon.

sections.heading: If your mic still does not work
items: Enable yapmod in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, then relaunch.
If yapmod is not listed there, run tccutil reset Microphone io.ilyeshdz.yapmod in Terminal and relaunch the app.

0.4.0.title: Themes and system tray
0.4.0.summary: This release adds system tray support, allowing yapmod to keep running in the background, and introduces custom theme support directly in the application.

sections.heading: New
items: System tray support lets yapmod keep running in the background when its window is closed, so desktop notifications continue while the window is hidden. This works on macOS, Windows, and most Linux desktop environments with tray indicators.
Custom themes can be loaded directly into yapmod from dedicated folders containing a CSS file and a manifest.json file. The format and requirements are documented on the documentation site.

0.4.1.title: Theme mode fixes
0.4.1.summary: Switch between light, dark, and system mode without reloading the app.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Theme mode changes now update the active styles without reloading the page.

0.5.0.title: Independent client updates and Windows fixes
0.5.0.summary: Yapmod adds support for separately versioned client updates and fixes a Windows startup issue that could keep its settings interface from loading correctly. This release also improves titlebar controls, settings navigation, theme startup, and topbar notifications.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Yapmod now supports client bundles published separately from desktop app releases. When a compatible update is available, it verifies the signed manifest and bundle hash, checks app compatibility, and stages the update. Yapmod then offers a restart to apply it; active calls will disconnect, and an update that fails to start is rolled back.

Fixed a Windows startup issue that could keep Yapmod's settings interface from loading correctly. Client startup now waits for the document root and head before installing its observers and styles, so the settings interface can integrate with Yapper's page.

Windows now has minimize, maximize or restore, and close controls in Yapper's top bar. Follow-up fixes restore button clicks and authorize the window commands. The host top bar also serves as the macOS window drag area.
Compact notification banners now appear in Yapper's top bar.

sections.heading: Improvements and fixes
items: Theme initialization waits until the document root exists, and injected styles wait until the page head is available. This makes startup styling more reliable.
Fixed settings navigation freezes caused by repeated event listeners and a mutation observer loop. Added icons to Yapmod's settings sections.
Updated Yapmod's Yapper integration for yapin.gg, including the supported bare and www addresses used to open the app and load the injected client.

sections.heading: Development and infrastructure
items: Daily and manually triggered nightly builds are now published as rolling prereleases for testing. Nightly builds may be unstable and do not have the stability guarantees of a stable release. They embed the client built from the same source revision.

Moved the injected client into its own client/ directory and added versioned, signed client release tooling. The embedded client in this release is version 1.0.2; client and desktop app versions remain separate and compatible versions are still required.

Unified the project checks, shared the app build workflow between stable and nightly packages, and improved portable and Windows MSI version handling. Removed unused Vite scaffolding and updated the website and desktop guides, including the AppImage limitation on some Wayland systems.

0.6.0.title: Community themes and plugins
0.6.0.summary: Yapmod v0.6.0 introduces community themes and the first version of the community plugin system, making it possible to customize Yapmod beyond what the desktop application provides out of the box. It also marks a major cleanup of the injected client, a new Solid.js-based architecture, and a separation of stable and nightly client updates to make releases easier to maintain.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Community themes are now supported through the Community Themes section. You can create your own themes and publish them for others to discover and use. The Yapmod website includes documentation explaining how to create a theme and submit it to the community collection.

The plugin system is now officially available, allowing developers to extend Yapmod using a dedicated plugin API. Community plugins can be published through a process similar to community themes. The system is still experimental, and the API documentation is currently minimal. Both the API and its documentation will continue to evolve as the system matures.

The first community plugin is already available: Custom Background. It lets you customize the application's background with an image of your choice and change the accent color. This plugin was developed to make extensive use of the new plugin API and serves as an initial example of what developers can build with it.

sections.heading: Improvements and fixes
items: The injected client has undergone a major internal refactor. Previously, much of the interface was built using native DOM manipulation and manually constructed strings. The client now uses Solid.js to handle UI components and DOM updates in a more structured way. This simplifies UI development and makes the codebase easier to maintain.

Styles that were previously embedded in JavaScript files have been moved into dedicated CSS files. The broader cleanup also removes unnecessary complexity and improves the structure of the client, laying the groundwork for more reliable future development.
Several adjustments have been made to improve the interface on macOS, continuing the work on making Yapmod feel more integrated with the platform.

sections.heading: Development and infrastructure
items: Stable and nightly releases now have independent client update channels, following an approach similar to Discord's stable and Canary clients. Previously, publishing a stable client update could depend on changes that were only available in the nightly development branch. Separating the two channels removes this dependency and allows each to evolve independently.

The main branch is now dedicated to stability, security fixes, hotfixes, and maintenance. It will not receive new experimental features as part of the normal development process. This keeps stable releases focused on reliability.

The nightly branch is dedicated to ongoing development and new features. Automated builds are published daily, giving users and developers access to the latest changes before they reach the stable channel. Nightly builds may be unstable and are intended for testing.

The plugin infrastructure is now in place, including an API designed specifically for plugin development and a community distribution process. However, the system is still experimental. Expect further improvements to the API, additional documentation, and changes as development continues.
